t: 2117. Abbreviating the Product of a Range
o: We need the product of [left, right] compressed to its first 5 digits, last 5 digits (after stripping trailing zeros), and the zero count C. Three quantities must be tracked streaming: (1) C and the last-5-digits residue — strip every factor 2 and 5 from each i, counting them separately (c2, c5) and multiplying the leftover cofactor into a mod-1e5 accumulator; at the end C = min(c2, c5) and the unmatched primes are multiplied back in; (2) the digit count via summing log10(i); (3) the exact product while it stays small — keep the zero-stripped product and abandon exact tracking once it exceeds 1e10, since a d <= 10 answer requires the stripped product to fit under 1e10. Example 2: 2..11 gives c2/c5 yielding C=2, stripped product 399168 with 6 digits, so output "399168e2".
k: Trailing zeros = min(count of factor 2, count of factor 5) across the whole product.
Track the product mod 100000 with all 2s and 5s stripped, then re-multiply the surplus prime to get the true last 5 digits.
Logarithms give the total digit count and the leading digits via the fractional part.
Keep an exact zero-stripped product only while it stays below 1e10 to handle the d <= 10 no-abbreviation case.

a.i: One pass maintains everything needed: exact small product, mod-1e5 stripped suffix, prime-surplus counts, and the log-sum for digit/leading-digit computation.
s: For each i: strip factors of 2 and 5 into counters, multiply the cofactor into suf mod 1e5, add log10(i), and grow the exact stripped product while it stays <= 1e10.
Compute C = min(c2, c5); multiply suf by the surplus prime (2^(c2-C) or 5^(c5-C)) mod 1e5.
Digits after stripping: d = floor(logSum) + 1 - C. If exact tracking never overflowed, return the exact stripped product with eC.
Otherwise prefix = floor(10^(frac+4)) from the log-sum fractional part; return "prefix...suf(padded to 5)eC".
a.t: O(right - left) — one pass with O(log i) prime stripping per number

w: This is the only practical approach without big integers. Pitfalls: the suffix must be zero-padded to 5 digits; the exact-product fallback must track the zero-stripped value (not the raw product) or the d <= 10 threshold is wrong; floating-point log precision is fine for 5 leading digits. Follow-up: how would you get the first 10 digits — keep more guard digits via higher-precision logs.
